# About Me

I am a hospitalist and addiction medicine physician at Johns Hopkins, where I am an Assistant Professor of Medicine in the Divisions of Hospital Medicine and Addiction Medicine. I care for hospitalized patients at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center, including on the inpatient substance use disorders consult service, and I teach medical students and residents. I am board certified in internal medicine and addiction medicine.

My research focuses on improving hospital care for people with opioid use disorder in the fentanyl era: how we manage withdrawal, how we start and dose methadone and buprenorphine, why patients leave the hospital before treatment is complete, and what systems-level changes help them stay connected to care. My work has been supported by an NIH KL2 career development award through the Johns Hopkins Institute for Clinical and Translational Research, a Center for Innovative Medicine Next Generation Scholars Award, and the Research in Addiction Medicine Scholars program. Earlier in my career I used real-world data to study emerging issues in COVID-19 and mpox, including the safety of Paxlovid in pregnancy and risk factors for severe mpox.

I am originally from Durham, North Carolina. I graduated from Yale, earned my MD and MPH at the University of North Carolina, and moved to Baltimore in 2016 for internal medicine residency at Johns Hopkins. In 2024 I completed an MHS through the [Graduate Training Programs in Clinical Investigation (GTPCI)](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/academics/academic-program-finder/graduate-training-programs-in-clinical-investigation "Graduate Training Programs in Clinical Investigation (GTPCI)") at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

You can find more about my [research](research/index.qmd) and my [CV](cv/index.qmd) on this site. Please feel free to [contact me](mailto:will.garneau@gmail.com) if you would like to discuss potential projects.
